title: Pallets that stay put: restraining bottled milk crates in fridge trucks and at the dock
summary: Every Monaro Milk load is palletised bottled milk in crates, carried in refrigerated HR trucks and semis. A pallet of milk is heavy, tall and sits on a smooth fridge floor, so if it is not properly wrapped, blocked or strapped it can slide or tip under braking or in a corner, and part-loads change after every drop. This week covers what the NHVR Load Restraint Guide 2025 says about general freight and pallets, how to keep the load secure on the run, and how to open fridge doors and unload safely at the dock.
key_risk: Pallets of bottled milk crates shifting, toppling or spilling inside the fridge body because they are poorly wrapped, not blocked, or left with gaps after drops. The NHVR Load Restraint Guide 2025 says a restraint system must hold 80 per cent of the load's weight forwards (braking) and half its weight sideways and rearwards, and that significant freight movement can affect vehicle stability or dislodge the load. A shifted pallet can also fall on someone when the rear doors are opened or during forklift unloading at the dock.
drivers_need_to_know: The law sets the forces, not the method. The NHVR Load Restraint Guide 2025 says the restraint must withstand 0.8 of the load's weight forwards, 0.5 sideways and 0.5 rearwards. Under hard braking a pallet tries to push forward with most of its own weight.

A fridge van body helps but does not do the job by itself. The Guide says containing mixed freight in a van is often easier than tie-down, but gaps must be filled: a cumulative gap of up to 200 mm front to back and up to 100 mm side to side is acceptable. Bigger gaps let pallets build speed and hit the walls or doors.

Wrap is not restraint on its own. The Guide says unitising (stretch wrap, strapping, banding) must hold the pallet together and stand up to forklift handling, but warns not to rely on unitising alone. Tall stacks can topple under heavy braking or cornering, putting extra force on the wrap.
Check the bottom layers too. The Guide warns that lower items left loose can come out of the pack. Torn or loose wrap, crushed or broken crates, or a leaning stack: get it fixed before you leave.
Part-loads change after every drop. Once pallets come off, the rest can have room to move. Re-block or re-strap with load bars, straps or empty pallets before you drive off from each delivery.
Don't use curtains or tarps as restraint unless they are engineered and rated for it (NHVR Load Restraint Guide 2025).
Drive for the load: brake early and smoothly, and take corners and roundabouts gently, especially when part loaded.

Opening the doors: the Guide says check the load for movement or stability before removing restraints and unloading. Open fridge doors slowly, stand to the side, and look before you reach in. If a pallet has shifted against the door, stop and get help.

At the dock: SafeWork NSW says workers are killed or hurt by being hit by a forklift, hit by its load, or in a tip-over, and that delivery drivers are most at risk walking between a forklift and a truck or helping load. Stay in the driver safety zone, keep line of sight with the forklift operator, and never steady a load by hand.

Secure the truck before loading or unloading (SafeWork NSW). Handbrake on, engine off as required by site rules, and check the dock plate is in place before any forklift or pallet jack goes into the trailer.
supervisors_must_check: Pallets leave the warehouse properly stretch-wrapped top to bottom, with no broken crates and a stable, squat stack.
Each truck and trailer has enough working load bars, straps or gates, and staff know where they are kept.
Loading follows a plan: heaviest pallets low and forward, gaps filled, and drop order planned so the remaining load can be re-secured.
The loader and driver agree who has authority and how loading will happen (NHVR Step 7), and the loading/unloading exclusion zone is marked at our dock.
Forklift operators hold a current LF high risk work licence, are on the licence register, and pre-start checks are done each shift (SafeWork NSW).
Fridge bodies: floors clean and dry (water and contaminants reduce friction), door seals, hinges and locks working, and internal restraint tracks undamaged.
Any load shift, spilt or broken crates, or damaged stock found at delivery is reported and looked into.
discussion_questions: When did you last open the doors and find a pallet had moved? What caused it?
After your first few drops, how do you stop the remaining pallets sliding around?
Do we have enough load bars and straps in every truck, and are any broken?
Where at our dock, or at customer sites, do you end up standing too close to a forklift?
What would you do if a pallet arrived from the warehouse badly wrapped or leaning?
practical_checklist: Pallets wrapped tight top to bottom, no loose or broken crates
Stacks upright, not leaning or overhanging the pallet
Pallets pushed up to the front, gaps no more than about 200 mm front to back and 100 mm side to side
Load bars, straps or gates fitted and tight
Fridge floor clean and dry before loading
Doors closed and latched, seals OK
Re-secure the remaining load after every drop
Truck secured and dock plate in place before forklift enters
Check for load movement before opening doors; open slowly and stand clear
Stay out of the forklift exclusion zone; keep eye contact with the operator
required_records: Toolbox talk sign-on register for this talk (this app's CSV export, or the printed register).
Daily pre-start checks for each truck and trailer, including fridge body doors, floor and load restraint equipment.
Forklift high risk work licence register and forklift pre-start check records.
Written loading and unloading procedure (with simple pallet layout diagrams) displayed at the dock.
Incident and near-miss reports for any load shift, fallen pallet, spilt stock or forklift near miss, with corrective actions.

follow_up_actions.action: Count and check load bars, straps and gates in every truck and trailer; replace damaged or missing items.
Write a one-page loading and unloading procedure with pallet layout diagrams and post it at the dock.
Mark the loading/unloading exclusion zone and driver safety zone at the dock.
Check the forklift HRW licence register is current for everyone who drives a forklift.
Follow up any load shift, wrap or dock concern raised in this talk.
